newsitem.title: USA: No signs of inflation in southeast US--Atlanta Fed.
newsitem.headline: No signs of inflation in southeast US--Atlanta Fed.

text.p: The manufacturing sector in the southeast of the United States is balanced with no significant signs of upward inflationary pressures, said Mark Rogers, an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta.

"Manufacturing is quite balanced in the southeast ... Prices remain relatively subdued and there is no significant sign of a pick-up of inflation in the sourtheast, at least for manufacturers," Rogers said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Rogers's remarks followed Wednesday's release of the Atlanta Fed diffusion index, which stood at 11.1 in January against a revised negative 18.7 in December.

"We had a very nice rebound from December, but we have a very well-balanced picture ... We clearly have some sharply higher numbers for current activity, but when you look at the detail, the numbers paint a picture of clear moderation in the southeast," Rogers said.

Rogers said the southeast economy, which has led the rest of the nation to some degree over much of the current economic expansion, appears to be running at a somewhat slower pace than the remainder of the U.S.
"The southeast (economy) currently seems to be a little bit slower than the rest of the country," Rogers said.
He added, however, that "for the nation, the picture for manufacturing does seem to be relatively healthy, with new orders volatile."
Rogers also said a strong dollar has been an "ongoing concern" for southeast exporters.
